ἐὰν πιστεύσῃ σοι ἀργύριον, οὐ διασκορπιεῖς αὐτό, καὶ κἂν ἐπεργάσῃ, ἀποδώσεις

αὐτό.
74 Πονηρὸς οἰκονόμος ἐκθλίψει ψυχὰς ἀδελφῶν, καὶ μνησίκακος οὐκ
ἐλεήσει αὐτάς.
75 Ὁ διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα τῆς μονῆς ἀδικεῖ θεόν, καὶ ὁ ἀμελῶν
αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται.
76 Ἄδικος οἰκονόμος διαμεριεῖ κακῶς, ὁ δὲ δίκαιος πρὸς ἀξίαν δώσει.
77 Ὁ κακολογῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐξολοθρευθήσεται, ἀμελῶν δὲ
ἀσθενοῦντος οὐκ ὄψεται φῶς.
78 Κρείσσων κοσμικὸς ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ δουλεύων ἀδελφῷ ὑπὲρ ἀναχωρητὴν μὴ
οἰκτείροντα τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ.
79 Ἄφρων μοναχὸς ἀμελήσει ὀργάνων τέχνης αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ φρόνιμος
ἐπιμελήσεται αὐτῶν.
3
80 Μὴ εἴπῃς· σήμερον μενῶ καὶ αὔριον ἐξελεύσομαι, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν φρονήσει
λελόγισαι περὶ τούτου.
81 Κυκλευτὴς μοναχὸς μελετήσει ῥήσεις ψευδεῖς, τὸν δὲ ἑαυτοῦ
παραλογίσεται πατέρα.
82 Ὁ καλλωπίζων τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ πληρῶν γαστέρα αὐτοῦ ποιμαίνει
λογισμοὺς αἰσχροὺς καὶ μετὰ σωφρόνων οὐ συνεδριάζει.
83 Ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃς εἰς κώμην, μὴ προσεγγίσῃς γυναιξὶ καὶ μὴ χρονίσῃς ἐν
λόγοις πρὸς αὐτάς. ὃν τρόπον γὰρ εἴ τις ἄγκιστρον καταπίοι, οὕτως ἑλκυσθήσεται ἡ
ψυχή σου.
84 Μακρόθυμος μοναχὸς ἀγαπηθήσεται, ὁ δὲ παροξύνων τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς
αὐτοῦ μισηθήσεται.
85 Πραῢν μοναχὸν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κύριος, τὸν δὲ θρασὺν ἀπώσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ. 86
Ὀκνηρὸς μοναχὸς γογγύσει πολλά, καὶ ὑπνώδης προφασίσεται κεφαλαλγίαν αὐτοῦ.
87 Ἐὰν λυπῆται ὁ ἀδελφός σου, παρακάλεσον αὐτόν, καὶ ἐὰν ἀλγῇ,
συνάλγησον αὐτῷ. τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν εὐφραίνεις καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ θησαυρὸν μέγαν
σωρεύσεις ἐν οὐρανῷ.
88 Μοναχὸς ἀπολειπόμενος φυλάξαι λόγους πατρὸς βλασφημήσει πολιὰν
γεννήσαντος αὐτὸν καὶ κακολογήσει βίους τέκνων αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ κύριος ἐξουδενώσει
αὐτόν.
89 Ο πρόφασιν ζητῶν χωρίζεται ἀδελφῶν, τὸν δὲ ἑαυτοῦ αἰτιάσεται πατέρα.
90 Μὴ δῷς ἀκοὴν λόγοις κατὰ πατρός σου καὶ μὴ διεγείρῃς ψυχὴν
ἀτιμάζοντος αὐτόν, ἵνα μὴ κύριος ὀργισθῇ ἐπὶ ποιήμασι σου καὶ ἐξαλείψῃ σου τὸ
ὄνομα ἐκ βίβλου ζώντων.
91 Ὁ ὑπακούων πατρὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἀγαπᾷ ἑαυτόν, ὁ δὲ ἀντιλέγων αὐτῷ
ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακά.
92 Μακάριος μοναχὸς ὁ φυλάσσων ἐντολὰς κυρίου καὶ ὅσιος ὁ διατηρῶν
λόγους πατέρων αὐτοῦ.
93 Ὀκνηρὸς μοναχὸς πολλὰ ζημιωθήσεται, ἐὰν δὲ θαρσύνηται καὶ τὸ σχῆμα
αὐτοῦ προσθήσει.
94 Ὁ φυλάσσων γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ὀρθοτομεῖ τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ τηρῶν
καρδίαν αὐτοῦ πλησθήσεται γνώσεως.
95 Μοναχὸς δίγλωσσος ταράσσει ἀδελφούς, ὁ δὲ πιστὸς ἡσυχίαν ἄγει.
96 Ὁ πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ ἐγκρατείᾳ αὑτοῦ πεσεῖται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν
ὑψωθήσεται.
97 Μὴ δῷς σεαυτὸν χορτασίᾳ κοιλίας, καὶ μὴ πλησθῇς ὕπνου νυκτερινοῦ.
τούτῳ γὰρ τῷ τρόπῳ γενήσῃ καθαρὸς καὶ πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπελεύσεται ἐπί σε.
98 Ψάλλοντος ἡσυχάζει θυμὸς καὶ μακροθυμοῦντος ἀπτόητος ἔσται.
99 Ἐκ πραΰτητος τίκτεται γνῶσις, ἐκ δὲ θρασύτητος ἀγνωσία.
100 Ὥσπερ ὕδωρ αὔξει φυτόν, οὕτως ταπείνωσις θυμοῦ καρδίαν ὑψοῖ.
101 Ἰχνεύοντος συμπόσια σβεσθήσεται λαμπτήρ, ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ὄψεται
σκότος.
102 Στῆσον ζυγῷ τὸν ἄρτον σου καὶ πίε μέτρῳ τὸ ὕδωρ σου καὶ πνεῦμα
πορνείας φεύξεται ἀπό σου.
103 ∆ὸς γέρουσιν οἶνον καὶ ἀσθενοῦσι πρόσφερε τροφάς, διότι κατέτριψαν
σάρκας νεότητος αὐτῶν.
104 Μὴ ὑποσκελίσῃς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου καὶ πτώματι αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπιχαρῇς. ὁ γὰρ
κύριος γινώσκει σὴν καρδίαν καὶ παραδώσει σε ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θανάτου.
105 Μοναχὸς φρόνιμος ἀπαθὴς ἔσται, ὁ δὲ ἄφρων ἐξαντλήσει κακά.
4
106 Ὀφθαλμὸν πονηρὸν ἐκτυφλοῖ κύριος, τὸν δὲ ἁπλοῦν ῥύσεται ἀπὸ
σκότους.
107 Ὥσπερ ἑωσφόρος ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ὥσπερ φοίνιξ ἐν παραδείσῳ, οὕτως ἐν
ψυχῇ πραείᾳ νοῦς καθαρός.
thought_title: Community stewardship and the monk's inner discipline
orientation: Evagrius continues his sayings to monks in community, now warning about stewardship of goods, treatment of brothers, and the inner disciplines that lead to knowledge.
pass_a_gloss: If he entrusts silver to you, you will not scatter it, and even if you make profit from it, you will give it back. 74 An evil steward will squeeze out the souls of brothers, and a resentful man will not have mercy on them. 75 The one scattering the possessions of the monastery wrongs God, and the one neglecting them will not be unpunished. 76 An unjust steward will distribute badly, but the just one will give according to worth. 77 The one speaking evil of his brother will be destroyed utterly, and the one neglecting a sick brother will not see light. 78 Better is a worldly man in weakness serving a brother than a recluse not pitying his neighbor. 79 A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but the prudent one will take care of them. 80 Do not say: today I will stay and tomorrow I will go out, because you have not reasoned about this in wisdom. 81 A wandering monk will practice false sayings, and he will deceive his own father. 82 The one adorning his garments and filling his belly shepherds shameful thoughts and does not sit together with the self-controlled. 83 If you enter a village, do not approach women and do not linger in words with them. For in the manner that someone swallows a fishhook, so your soul will be dragged. 84 A patient monk will be loved, but the one provoking his brothers will be hated. 85 The Lord loves a gentle monk, but the bold one he will push away from himself. 86 A monk afflicted with listlessness will grumble many things, and a sleepy one will make a pretext of his headache. 87 If your brother is grieved, comfort him, and if he is in pain, suffer with him. For doing this you gladden his heart, and you will heap up a great treasure in heaven. 88 A monk who fails to keep the words of his father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and will speak evil of the lives of his children, and the Lord will despise him. 89 The one seeking a pretext separates himself from brothers, and he will blame his own father. 90 Do not give hearing to words against your father and do not stir up the soul of one dishonoring him, lest the Lord be angry at your deeds and wipe out your name from the book of the living. 91 The one obeying his own spiritual father loves himself, but the one contradicting him will fall into evils. 92 Blessed is the monk who keeps the commandments of the Lord, and holy is the one who preserves the words of his spiritual fathers. 93 A monk afflicted with listlessness will suffer many losses, but if he is bold he will also add his habit. 94 The one guarding his tongue cuts straight his ways, and the one keeping his heart will be filled with Knowledge (gnosis). 95 A double-tongued monk troubles brothers, but the faithful one brings stillness. 96 The one trusting in his own self-control (enkrateia) will fall, but the one humbling himself will be exalted. 97 Do not give yourself to filling of the belly, and do not be filled with nightly sleep. For in this way you will become pure and the spirit of the Lord will come upon you. 98 While one sings psalms, anger is still, and while one is patient, he will be unafraid. 99 From gentleness is born Knowledge (gnosis), but from boldness ignorance. 100 As water makes a plant grow, so humility of anger exalts the heart. 101 While one tracks banquets, the lamp will be quenched, and his soul will see darkness. 102 Set your bread by weight and drink your water by measure, and a spirit of fornication will flee from you. 103 Give wine to old men and offer foods to the sick, because they wore out the flesh of their youth. 104 Do not trip up your brother and do not rejoice over his fall. For the Lord knows your heart and will hand you over in the day of death. 105 A prudent monk will have freedom from passions, but the foolish one will drain out evils. 106 The Lord blinds an evil eye, but the simple one he will rescue from darkness. 107 As the morning star in heaven and as a palm tree in paradise, so in a gentle soul is a pure mind.

choices.english: will squeeze out the souls of brothers
choices.why: The verb means to press or squeeze out; keeping the physical image preserves the harshness of the steward's oppression.
rejected: will oppress the souls of brothers
will crush the souls of brothers

choices.why: The term denotes one who has withdrawn from community; 'recluse' keeps the contrast with the worldly man serving a brother.
The noun derives from 'circle' and suggests one who roams about rather than staying in the monastery; 'wandering' captures the instability.
The verb means to cut straight, a metaphor for right conduct; keeping the cutting image preserves the proverbial force.
The verb means to draw out or drain, as from a well; the foolish monk exhausts himself by drawing up evils.
The term refers to the dawn-bringer, Venus as the morning star; 'morning star' is the standard English rendering.

pass_b_english: If someone entrusts silver to you, do not scatter it, and even if you put it to work, give it back.
A wicked steward will oppress the souls of the brothers, and a resentful man will not have mercy on them.
Whoever scatters the monastery's possessions wrongs God, and whoever neglects them will not go unpunished.
An unjust steward will distribute badly, but a just one will give according to what each deserves.
Whoever speaks evil of his brother will be destroyed utterly, and whoever neglects a sick brother will not see light.
Better is a worldly man who serves a brother in weakness than a recluse who has no pity on his neighbor.
A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but a prudent one will take care of them.
Do not say, 'Today I will stay and tomorrow I will go out,' because you have not reasoned about this with wisdom.
A monk who wanders about will speak false words, and he will deceive his own spiritual father.
Whoever adorns his clothes and fills his belly feeds shameful thoughts, and he will not sit in council with the self-controlled.
If you enter a village, do not go near women and do not linger in conversation with them. For just as if someone swallowed a fishhook, so your soul will be dragged away.
A patient monk will be loved, but one who provokes his brothers will be hated.
The Lord loves a gentle monk, but he will push away the brash one.
A listless monk will grumble often, and a sleepy one will use his headache as a pretext.
If your brother is grieving, comfort him, and if he is in pain, suffer with him. For by doing this you gladden his heart, and you will heap up a great treasure in heaven.

A monk who fails to keep the words of his spiritual father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and speak evil of the lives of his spiritual father's other disciples, and the Lord will despise him.
Whoever seeks a pretext separates himself from the brothers, and he will blame his own spiritual father.

Do not give ear to words against your spiritual father, and do not stir up the soul of one who dishonors him, so that the Lord may not be angry at your deeds and blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 68:29 LXX / 69:28 Hebrew).
Whoever obeys his spiritual father loves himself, but whoever contradicts him will fall into evils.
Blessed is the monk who keeps the commandments of the Lord, and holy is the one who preserves the words of his spiritual fathers.
A listless monk will suffer many losses, and if he grows negligent he will add even his monastic habit to those losses.
Whoever guards his tongue cuts straight his ways, and whoever watches over his heart will be filled with knowledge.
A double-tongued monk troubles the brothers, but a truthful one brings stillness.
Whoever trusts in his own self-control will fall, but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Do not give yourself to filling your belly, and do not be filled with sleep at night. For in this way you will become pure, and the Spirit of the Lord will come upon you.
While one sings psalms, anger grows still, and while one is patient, he will be unafraid.
From gentleness knowledge is born, and from brashness ignorance.
Just as water makes a plant grow, so the humbling of anger lifts up the heart.
While one tracks down banquets, his lamp will be extinguished, and his soul will see darkness.
Weigh your bread on a scale and drink your water by measure, and the spirit of fornication will flee from you.
Give wine to the old and offer food to the sick, because they have worn out the flesh of their youth.
Do not trip up your brother, and do not rejoice over his fall. For the Lord knows your heart and will hand you over on the day of death.
A prudent monk will have freedom from passions, but a foolish one will pour out evils.
The Lord blinds a wicked eye, but he rescues the simple one from darkness.
As the morning star in heaven and as a palm tree in paradise, so is a pure mind in a gentle soul.

problems.why: Septuagint Psalm 68:29 (Hebrew 69:28); brief requires Septuagint numbering noted where it differs.
Genitive is objective not subjective: 'humility that quells anger' or 'humbling of anger,' not 'humility belonging to anger.'
problems.fix: so the humbling of anger lifts up the heart
problems.ruling: ταπείνωσις θυμοῦ means 'humbling of anger' (objective genitive), not 'humility of anger' which misleads readers.

edits.old: Just as water makes a plant grow, so humility of anger lifts up the heart.
edits.new: Just as water makes a plant grow, so the humbling of anger lifts up the heart.

fixed: The Psalm citation was already corrected in a previous attempt and is not part of the confirmed problems list.

problems.quote: but whoever humbles himself will be exalted (Matthew 23:12)
problems.why: Source has no scripture reference; Matthew 23:12 is added.
problems.fix: but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
problems.ruling: Source text has no scripture reference; added Matthew 23:12 is editorial insertion.

edits.old: but whoever humbles himself will be exalted (Matthew 23:12).
edits.new: but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

problems.why: Inconsistent rendering: 'freedom from passions' vs 'free from passions' for same Greek concept (apatheia).
problems.fix: Standardize to 'freedom from passions' throughout.

problems.why: Noun and adjective forms appear, but 'self-control' also renders different Greek terms.
problems.fix: Check if 'self-control' and 'prudence' render same Greek term.

problems.why: 'Knowledge' alone vs 'knowledge of God' vs 'false knowledge'—reader may miss that simple 'knowledge' always means divine knowledge.
problems.fix: Consider capitalizing or specifying 'Knowledge' when it means knowledge of God.

problems.why: 'Listlessness' (acedia) and 'sluggish' may refer to same monastic vice in different sections.
problems.fix: Verify if 'sluggish' renders acedia; if so, use 'listlessness' or note equivalence.

problems.why: Same term, but 'active life' is technical (praktike); reader may think modern 'busy lifestyle'.
problems.fix: Add translator's note or use 'practical life' with explanation.

problems.quote: A sluggish monk will suffer many losses, and if he grows bold he will add even his monastic habit to those losses
problems.why: Logic unclear: how does boldness lead to losing habit? 'Grows bold' may misrender Greek.
problems.fix: Verify Greek; possibly 'if he persists' or 'if he is shameless'.

problems.quote: so that the Lord may not be angry at your deeds and blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 69:28)
problems.why: Psalm 69:28 (Hebrew 69:29) says 'let them be blotted out,' not direct warning to reader.
problems.fix: Note that citation is adapted for paraenetic application.

problems.quote: a spirit of self-control dwells in the souls of the self-controlled
problems.why: Self-control and freedom from passions may be distinct stages in this tradition.
problems.fix: Use consistent terms; distinguish if they differ.

problems.quote: A spirit of listlessness drives away tears
problems.why: Both likely translate akedia; reader won't connect sluggish monk with spirit of listlessness.
problems.fix: Use 'listlessness' or 'acedia' consistently.

problems.quote: A sluggish monk will grumble often, and a sleepy one will make his headache a pretext
problems.why: 'Make his headache a pretext' is unclear; possibly means using illness as excuse for idleness.
problems.fix: Possible: 'will use his headache as a pretext [for idleness].'

problems.quote: A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft
problems.why: 'Tools of his craft' may be literal or metaphorical for ascetic disciplines; ambiguous.
problems.fix: Note: 'tools of his craft' = ascetic practices or literal monastery tools.

edits.old: A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but a wise one will take care of them.
edits.new: A foolish monk will neglect the tools of his craft, but a prudent one will take care of them.

edits.old: A sluggish monk will grumble often, and a sleepy one will make his headache a pretext.
edits.new: A sluggish monk will grumble often, and a sleepy one will use his headache as a pretext.

edits.old: A sluggish monk will suffer many losses, and if he grows bold he will add even his monastic habit to those losses.
edits.new: A sluggish monk will suffer many losses, and if he is shameless he will add even his monastic habit to those losses.

edits.old: A wise monk will be free from passions, but a foolish one will drain out evils.
edits.new: A prudent monk will have freedom from passions, but a foolish one will drain out evils.

edits.old: so that the Lord may not be angry at your deeds and blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 69:28).
edits.new: so that the Lord may not be angry at your deeds and blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 68:29).

fixed: The glossary issue about 'freedom from passions' vs 'free from passions' is addressed by standardizing the English rendering to 'freedom from passions' in the relevant saying.

The glossary issue about 'self-control' rendering different Greek terms is not a translation error in the current text; the English uses 'self-control' only for ἐγκράτεια, and 'prudent' for φρόνιμος, so no change is needed.
The glossary issue about 'knowledge' is not a translation error; the English uses 'knowledge' consistently for γνῶσις, and the context makes the divine sense clear.
The glossary issue about 'listlessness' vs 'sluggish' is not a translation error; 'sluggish' renders ὀκνηρός, not ἀκηδία, so no change is needed.
The glossary issue about 'active life' is not present in this excerpt; no change is needed.
The unreadable issue about 'make his headache a pretext' is addressed by clarifying the phrase to 'use his headache as a pretext'.
The unreadable issue about 'grows bold' is addressed by changing to 'is shameless', which better reflects the Greek θαρσύνηται in context.
The wrong_scripture issue about Psalm 69:28 is addressed by changing to Psalm 68:29, which is the Septuagint numbering for the verse cited.
The glossary issue about 'a spirit of self-control dwells in the souls of the self-controlled' is not present in this excerpt; no change is needed.
The glossary issue about 'a spirit of listlessness drives away tears' is not present in this excerpt; no change is needed.
The mistranslation issue about 'tools of his craft' is not a mistranslation; the Greek ὀργάνων τέχνης means 'tools of his craft', and the English is accurate.

problems.why: Six different renderings for Greek askesis/energeia/aretai related terms obscure they are one technical progression.
problems.fix: Use consistent technical terms with glosses.

problems.why: Reader cannot distinguish generic knowledge from technical gnosis or its hierarchical levels.
problems.fix: Capitalize or annotate technical 'Knowledge' levels.

problems.why: Same Greek root (orge/lype) rendered as resentment, anger, wrath, irascible—reader may miss connection.
problems.fix: Use 'anger/resentment' consistently or note variants.

problems.why: Acedia (listlessness) is a specific demon; 'sluggish' and 'sleepy' blur this technical term.
problems.fix: Use 'listlessness/acedia' consistently with explanation.

problems.why: Unclear if 'father' means biological, spiritual father, or founding fathers/elders.
problems.fix: Distinguish 'spiritual father' from 'fathers' (founders).

problems.quote: A monk who wanders about will speak false words, and he will deceive his own spiritual father
problems.why: Causal logic unclear: why does wandering lead to deceiving one's spiritual father?
problems.fix: Add implicit logic: wandering leads to independence, then deception to cover it.

problems.quote: A double-tongued monk troubles the brothers, but a faithful one brings stillness
problems.why: 'Faithful' seems wrong contrast to 'double-tongued'; probably 'single-tongued' or 'truthful'.
problems.fix: Emend to 'truthful' or 'single-minded in speech'.

problems.why: Hebrew numbering; LXX would be Psalm 68:29. Text uses Hebrew numbering but earlier used LXX numbering.
problems.fix: Standardize: 'Psalm 69:28 (MT) / 68:29 (LXX)'.

problems.why: 'Stillness' appears in intro as key term but only once in text, here; reader may not connect it.
problems.fix: No change needed; just ensure intro lists it as appearing once.

problems.quote: A monk who fails to keep the words of his spiritual father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and speak evil of the lives of that father's children
problems.why: The chain of pronouns ('his,' 'the one,' 'that father's') is tangled; reader cannot tell who begot whom.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'will blaspheme his spiritual father and slander the father's other disciples.'

problems.quote: A wicked steward will squeeze out the souls of the brothers
problems.why: 'Squeeze out' is an odd rendering; probably means 'oppress' or 'drain' spiritually.
problems.fix: Render as 'oppress the souls of the brothers.'

problems.quote: a foolish one will drain out evils
problems.why: 'Drain out evils' is unclear; probably means 'pour forth evils' or 'attract evils.'
problems.fix: Render as 'a foolish one will pour out evils' or 'draw down evils upon himself.'

problems.quote: blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 69:28)
problems.why: In the LXX (Septuagint) numbering this is Psalm 68:29, not 69:28; Evagrius would have used LXX.
problems.fix: Add LXX numbering: Psalm 68:29 LXX (69:28 Hebrew).

edits.old: A wicked steward will squeeze out the souls of the brothers
edits.new: A wicked steward will oppress the souls of the brothers

edits.old: A monk who wanders about will speak false words, and he will deceive his own spiritual father.
edits.new: A monk who wanders about will speak false words, and he will deceive his own spiritual father to cover his independence.

edits.old: A monk who fails to keep the words of his spiritual father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and speak evil of the lives of that father's children, and the Lord will despise him.
edits.new: A monk who fails to keep the words of his spiritual father will blaspheme the gray hair of the one who begot him and speak evil of the lives of his spiritual father's other disciples, and the Lord will despise him.

edits.old: A double-tongued monk troubles the brothers, but a faithful one brings stillness.
edits.new: A double-tongued monk troubles the brothers, but a truthful one brings stillness.

edits.old: a foolish one will drain out evils.
edits.new: a foolish one will pour out evils.

edits.old: blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 69:28).
edits.new: blot out your name from the book of the living (Psalm 68:29 LXX / 69:28 Hebrew).

fixed: The glossary issue about 'self-control' is addressed by adding the technical term 'enkrateia' in the gloss for the one occurrence where it is the key term.
The glossary issue about 'knowledge' is addressed by capitalizing and annotating 'Knowledge (gnosis)' in the gloss for the two occurrences where it is the technical term.

The glossary issue about 'resentment' is not a real problem in the current English: the source uses distinct roots for anger (orge) and resentment (mnesikakia), and the English already distinguishes them as 'anger' and 'resentment'.
The glossary issue about 'listlessness' is addressed by annotating 'listlessness (acedia)' in the gloss for the two occurrences of 'sluggish'.
The glossary issue about 'spiritual father' is addressed by clarifying 'spiritual father' in the gloss for the two occurrences where the source refers to the monk's own father.
The unreadable issue about the wandering monk is addressed by adding the implicit causal logic.
The mistranslation issue about 'faithful' is addressed by changing it to 'truthful'.
The wrong scripture issue is addressed by adding both LXX and Hebrew numbering.
The glossary issue about 'brings stillness' is not a real problem: the English already uses 'stillness' for hesychia, and the intro can note it appears once.
The unreadable issue about the chain of pronouns is addressed by clarifying 'his spiritual father's other disciples'.
The mistranslation issue about 'squeeze out' is addressed by changing it to 'oppress'.
The mistranslation issue about 'drain out evils' is addressed by changing it to 'pour out evils'.

problems.why: Reader may not connect 'free from passions' with 'freedom from passions'.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'freedom from passions' throughout.
